correctness.rationale: The lift to the infinite fence forces increments in {-1,0,1}, gives the degree bound, and forces zero runs between nonzero increments to be even. Explicit pointwise-comparability moves cancel opposite increments and slide zero pairs through unit steps. They reduce every nonextremal map to one degree class and transport its phase. Equality in the degree bound forces a same-sign unit-step word, giving exactly n isolated maps per extremal sign. The packaged finite enumerator independently reproduces the predicted components in five representative cases.

originality.rationale: The inspected crown-enumeration papers count order-preserving maps rather than finite-space homotopy classes. Cavallo--Sattler define crown winding and prove the shorter-to-longer zero-winding lemma, not the all-parameter classification. Čukić--Kozlov give the closest analogue for graph Hom complexes of cycles, but their maps forbid edge collapse; their statement does not imply the finite-space classification without the collapse-and-slide bridge. value.rationale: Crown posets are standard finite circle models, so maps between them are a natural test of finite-space homotopy. The theorem completely gives the realizable winding degrees and exact homotopy-class count for every pair of sizes, while identifying a sharp divisibility boundary where maximal winding becomes rigid. This unifies the shorter-to-longer and self-map phenomena in a structural two-parameter classification rather than an arbitrary finite census.
